correctness.rationale: Every distance in K_n x K_n is 1 when both coordinates differ and 2 when exactly one agrees (n>=3). For any cut, exact separated-pair counts give A=2U/[n²(n−1)], B=2V/[n²(n−1)], C=2(T−U−V)/[n²(n−1)²]. The exact identity 2(n−1)C−(n−2)(A+B)=2/[n(n−1)] times the two row/column variance sums is nonnegative, with equality precisely for regular cuts. Integrating over nonnegative cut weights proves the lower bound. The explicit permutation-coordinate embedding realizes all pair distances with equality. Extremal distance-profile and supporting-cut rigidity follow from equality throughout. A standalone standard-library checker replayed successfully: 8755 breadth-first distances, 80088 cut certificates, and 1086 exact-rational embedding pairs. Finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The least L1 distortion is an intrinsic, natural metric-embedding invariant of the infinite strongly regular family of complements of square lattice/rook graphs. The exact formula gives a sharp isometric-to-nonisometric transition at n=3 and approaches 2; a universal sharp sum-of-squares cut inequality classifies all equality-supporting cuts as regular bipartite incidence patterns and forces every optimal image distance. Those structural classifications make the fact useful beyond a numerical computation and are not implied by the nearest inspected qualitative gate-sum or generic embedding results. Rectangular products and general weighted cases remain open in this proof.
